b: The one east-side Pilates girls keep rating 10/10. A spacious reformer studio with mirrors on every wall so you can actually check your form.
tip: A Lemon8 reviewer flagged the first-timer trial at $88 for 5 sessions. Confirm the current offer when you book.

b: A collab between The Flow Studio and Lab Studios. Reformer, barre and yoga in a shophouse, with showers so you can go straight to brunch.
tip: Newbies have been offered 2 classes for $40. Reformer Foundations is the gentle way in.

b: Lab Studios' East Coast Road home, upstairs opposite i12 Katong. It is one of the most-reviewed studios in the area on ClassPass.
A big reformer and Wunda chair studio on level three of i12 Katong, from the Absolute Boutique Fitness family.
tip: Trial has been listed at $42 for two classes.

b: A shared home for independent trainers, physios and wellness pros, so one address covers many kinds of class.
A calm studio on Tanjong Katong Road with thousands of glowing ClassPass reviews for both yoga and reformer.
For when you want the teacher's full attention. Solo and duet sessions on the full set of apparatus.
Pioneers of Pilates and Gyrotonic in Singapore, training everyone from athletes to first-timers.
tip: A private trial has been listed at $75.

b: The Australian fast-paced reformer format. Fifty minutes and you will feel all of them.
A small upstairs Pilates studio on the north stretch of Joo Chiat Road.
Honeycombers' pick for beginners. A huge range of reformer, chair and tower classes at every level.
A wellness studio at Katong Point listed for reformer classes.
Indoor climbing walls inside a mall. No experience needed and no rain can cancel it.
tip: Go with friends and race each other up.

b: The east side's lululemon, more than 3,000 square feet of it. The store also hosts community runs.
tip: Follow the store's run club. Community runs have started here on weekend mornings.

b: An ActiveSG public pool tucked in a quiet estate. Laps for a couple of dollars.
High-end vintage from the 1950s to the 1990s under a pink neon sign. The Kilo Tale corner sells by weight, and there is a hidden bar at the back.
A small vintage shop that Eatbook slotted into its perfect Katong day.
A quirky indie store with a resident cat. Books, stationery and Singapore-themed trinkets by local designers.
tip: The best place in Katong for a gift that is not boring.

b: New and pre-loved vinyl, plus turntables and speakers. Band tees live a few doors down at Good Vibes.
A Singapore label known for clean, architectural womenswear, in a three-storey shophouse. Miura's matcha bar is hidden inside.
Part gallery, part shop for local artists' merchandise and vintage finds.
A breezy clothing boutique on the southern stretch of Joo Chiat Road.
A colourful boutique with resort-style clothes and accessories.
A collective of ethical and sustainable brands under one roof.
Your tropical-home Pinterest board as a shop: prints, art and wall decor.
A design furniture showroom you can wander like a gallery. Accompany Coffee is inside.
A speciality cheese counter for building the perfect picnic platter.
tip: Pick up cheese here, then picnic at East Coast Park.

b: An old-school rattan and cane furniture shop, a survivor from the Joo Chiat of decades ago.

n: Vintage Flea Market by The Retro Factory
b: A monthly vintage market in front of Katong Square. The vendors rotate, so every visit is different.
tip: It runs on the first Friday-to-Sunday of the month.
hrs: Fri-Sat 1-10pm, Sun 11am-8pm (first weekend of the month)

b: The Japanese second-hand fashion chain. Racks of pre-loved streetwear and designer bags.
An upstairs lash studio on East Coast Road.
A brow embroidery studio at The Flow.
A Joo Chiat hair salon popular with the neighbourhood's expat crowd.
An award-winning reflexology spot. Exactly what your feet want after a day of cafe-hopping.
A second-floor creative studio and art cafe. Paint a figurine or make DIY charms, with sessions from $18.
tip: A low-key date that is not just another coffee.

b: Pick a ceramic piece, paint it your way and collect it once it is glazed.
tip: Brunch at The Brewing Ground in the same compound first.

b: Hand-building and wheel-throwing with a close-knit community of potters. Trial lessons run about 2.5 hours.
Calming two-hour craft sessions such as tapestry weaving.
A cosy 16-seat studio for art workshops and private events.
Try Peranakan beading, taste kueh with tea, or dress up in a kebaya for a studio shoot.
tip: Studio shoots have been listed from $60 a person. Workshops need a group.

b: The neighbourhood cinema on the top floor of i12 Katong.
A multiplex on level five of PLQ Mall. K.STAR Karaoke is on the same floor.
An indoor ice rink for the hottest days. Leisure Park Kallang also has bowling and a cinema.
The giant dome where the big concerts happen. Even with no ticket, the breezy waterfront loop around it is a great run or sunset walk.
A low-rise campus of artist studios, galleries and dance spaces in a former school.
The candy-coloured row you have seen on every feed. Two facing terraces built in the 1920s and 30s with Peranakan tiles, plaster flowers and pintu pagar doors.
tip: Shoot before 9am for soft light and empty pavements. People live here, so stay on the walkway.

b: A pastel pink building with serious Wes Anderson energy.
Once the Katong Bakery & Confectionery, where generations bought Swiss rolls and curry puffs. The red facade was restored and now houses cafes.
A private terrace house filled floor to ceiling with one collector's Peranakan antiques. Tours come with tea and stories from the owner.
tip: By appointment only, so book ahead.

b: A shophouse museum of Baba-Nyonya life, with portraits, wedding costumes and porcelain.
tip: Call ahead for a guided visit.

b: The story of Singapore's Eurasian community, told at the Eurasian Community House.
One of Singapore's oldest Hindu temples, with a towering Chola-style gateway covered in sculpted deities.
tip: Dress modestly and leave your shoes outside.

b: The Katong parish church, long tied to the neighbourhood's Eurasian and Peranakan Catholic families.
A neighbourhood mosque that has stood on Joo Chiat Road since the early 1900s.
A century-old temple dedicated to Guanyin, with a classic curved roof among the terraces.
Ernest Zacharevic's much-loved mural of two kids jousting on painted horses, on a corner wall.
Fifteen kilometres of beach, palms and cycling track. It is five minutes from Katong and where the whole east comes to exhale.
tip: Sunrise is at about 7am all year. Bring a mat and a coffee.

b: A four-storey play tower with slides and a water-play area, on the site of the old Big Splash.
A big lawn ringed by restaurants and cafes, with a dog run next door.
The classic East Coast meet-up point, with a giant playground, a famous McDonald's and beach on the doorstep.
Purpose-built bike circuits and a learn-to-ride area. Bike rental shops are dotted along the park.
tip: Rentals start at around $8 an hour.

b: Bowls and street courses built to international competition standards, right by the sea.
Cable-ski a lagoon without needing a boat. Beginners are welcome.
tip: Passes have started from about $50 an hour.

b: A long jetty reaching out to sea. Anglers, cyclists and the best horizon in the east.
One of Singapore's oldest parks. The remains of a 19th-century fort are buried under the lawn.
A small park with a wave-shaped vertical playground wrapped in netting.
Katong's main mall after its big revamp. lululemon, PS.Cafe, a climbing gym, Pilates studios, a cinema and a basement of snacks.
tip: Lululemon is on level 1, Pilates on level 3, climbing on 4 and the cinema on 5.

b: The east's classic big mall, linked to Marine Parade MRT. UNIQLO, MUJI, MANGO, Cotton On, KKV, Shake Shack and a full beauty hall.
tip: Chanel, Kiehl's and Clarins counters are on level 1.

b: A retro strata mall of small independent shops, salons, tuition centres and studios beside the Grand Mercure Roxy hotel. It is best known for the original Janggut Laksa on level one.
tip: Roxy Square publishes no store directory, so the list here is partial. It comes from listings and community mapping.

b: A small mall under Village Hotel Katong with cafes, a FairPrice Finest and private Pilates upstairs.
Singapore's first air-conditioned mall and still gloriously retro. Come for chicken rice and banana pie, stay for hobby shops and hidden coffee.
A dining cluster built around the former Joo Chiat Police Station, with Hotel Indigo and Holiday Inn Express above.
A small mall beside Katong Square with coffee, beauty studios and enrichment centres.
The corner of Joo Chiat Road and East Coast Road, with Little Farms and Pilates studios.
A low-key complex that has quietly turned into a cafe row.
A Paya Lebar mall with a huge Daiso and budget fashion.
Paya Lebar Quarter's bright modern mall. UNIQLO, 2nd STREET thrift, Novela and innisfree for beauty, a Starbucks Reserve and a Shaw cinema.
The mall across from PLQ, linked to Paya Lebar MRT.
A mall next to Paya Lebar MRT with a cinema and a big food line-up.
An old-school mall packed with wholesale fashion shops, and home to the famous Arnold's Fried Chicken.
tip: Bring cash and patience. It rewards digging.

b: The place for fabric, baju kurung and Hari Raya shopping.
The mall beside the National Stadium, with sports stores and an indoor climbing wall.
The big heartland mall above Bedok MRT and bus interchange.
A design hotel themed on Peranakan Katong, rising behind the old police station, with a rooftop infinity pool.
A hair salon on level one of Roxy Square.
The quiet side of Gardens by the Bay. A waterfront lawn with the full Marina Bay skyline across the water.
tip: Best at blue hour. It is at the far edge of this map, so cycle or take a bus.

b: Swim laps in the national competition pool at the Sports Hub.
Rent a kayak or pedal boat and paddle the Kallang Basin with the stadium dome behind you.
